item.title: Strange
item.content:encoded:
SCP-722 was found in the eastern glacial ranges of Greenland by Greenpeace activists making a documentary on the effects of global warming. Upon descending into a crevasse that had opened up on the southern end of the Kangerdlugssuaq glacier, they discovered a network of tunnels within the glacier which had long since been smoothed out, eventually reaching a series of larger chambers which seemed to host a tremendous serpentine body. After another hour of exploration the team left the glacier and headed to the nearby town of ██████████. Within hours most of the team felt symptoms of a wide array of sicknesses resembling everything from swollen lymph nodes to fast necrosis of the skin. By nightfall the entire team was dead. An SCP operative on leave caught wind of the story and sent notification to high command.

That part feels out of place in the description, (and the style is off with the rest of the article. EDIT : after several readings, not that much )

Was it added after ?

item.content:encoded:
The primary issue I have with this one is that it speaks to much to people already familiar with SCPs, i.e. foundation members. Stuff like "our labs", or references to "while this would normally warrant Euclid status" or whatever the exact words were. The note reminding readers that the object is Keter, as opposed to explaining exactly why it is, doesn't help; it all feels just a bit like it was written by someone trying to show their familiarity with the Foundation by writing a Keter SCP rather than someone trying to just write a good Keter SCP.

The "agent on leave" thing has already been noted.

Danger alone does not a Keter make. Keter SCPs are Keter because they pose an active danger to all humans that would be unleashed if not restrained by the Foundation or similar. A very dangerous thing that merely has to be locked up to keep it from doing harm is not Keter. Similarly, a cold-blooded monster frozen in a glacier is not Keter because the only thing necessary to keep it dormant would be to keep everyone away and install artificial refrigeration if the global temperature actually increased too much.

Downvoting until rewritten by someone who's reviewed the Rules of Thumb for some style tips.

Edit: reread, apparently artificial refrigeration is already in effect. Still, details like "silenced flechette pistol" or "terminated with extreme prejudice regardless of security clearance" make it feel like it's trying to be the setting for an impending action movie or something. Also "extremely volatile" is not the phrase to use when describing something one should avoid touching due to its toxicity; you're thinking of explosives. "Volatile" =/= "dangerous".

item.content:encoded:
Facing the danger of necroposting, I'd like to contribute a bit to the 'Nordic Script' part of this SCP, since it's extremely vague. It only says that it predates Eriks colony in the 11th century. However, vikings reportedly lived in Iceland from about 860. That's actually quite a bit closer to that glacier than Eriks settlement was.
Furthermore, ancient Nordic runes have a name, specifically the elder futhark, a runic alphabet that probably dates back to year 0+/-100 years. Said alphabet contains similarities with ancient Greek and Etruskian, plus other ancient Mediterranean alphabets. Usually, people take this to mean that since Germanians talked to the Romans, Latin writing influenced the emerging futhark, but it could also mean the runes are simply old as hell. I'd suggest something like:

"Most of the tunnels in SCP-722's enclosure are completely smooth, though a few patches, specifically on the paths nearest to the head and tail of the artifact, are marked with runes resembling those of the elder futhark, an alphabet used in Germania until the 7th-9th century. Few of them correspond directly to the runes found in this alphabet, however, and thus no text has yet been verifiably translated. Since the earliest confirmed settlement of Greenland or the neighboring Iceland by Nordics, the most likely source of the runic alphabet, didn't happen until the 9th century, dating the runes has proven difficult."

item.title: Location question/change
item.content:encoded: The location listed for this is Site-103. There is a Bio Site-103 already listed in the Secure Facilities Locations section surrounding SCP-757, and as the Site-103 for SCP-722 appears to be a glacier, it's unlikely that they are one in the same. I would recommend changing the Site number. As it appears to be a recent discovery (reference to Greenpeace) I'd say a higher number. My own list is incomplete, but has more than the Secure Facilities Locations section, and it looks like Sites 94-102, then 105-287 are unused.

item.content:encoded: I agree with mrunimport. This is extremely similar to scp 169. The unkown size, current hibernatory state and the fact that leviathan (169) and jormungandr (722) are huge serpentine monstrosities points to an accidental copy scp. Regarding 722 itself i feel as though it focuses too heavily on the poison and less on the sheer size of the beast. I find that The poison itself is overpowered to the point of breaking my natural suspension of disbelief. It has no cure, cannot be avoided and produces random effects to kill someone. If the poison was an scp in and of itself it would be more impressive. Also if it is so unstable outside of 722 that it cannot be recovered for study it would also degrade too quickly to effectively poison someone. I am sorry to say that there are too many issues at this point for me to upvote this scp.
